risks: Repairing operator RTL now would target symptoms without an executed failing RTL transaction and could contaminate the smallest repairable boundary.

Filling in or loosening atol, rtol, or max_mismatch_fraction inside the current repair loop would alter immutable numeric policy. The missing tolerance requires an approved Stage6 backtrack and a new immutable verification contract.
Copying hashes from the rejected Stage7 manifests without regenerating and checking complete-scope bindings could falsely claim that the DUT consumed the checkpoint weights.

Using random expected outputs, RTL-derived outputs, an identity/default target model, or fallback stage harnesses would invalidate functional evidence. Random generation is allowed only for input stimulus, and expected outputs must come from the real target model on the same immutable checkpoint and stimulus.
Expanding DUT tensor coverage to embeddings, final norm, LM head/logits, or sampling to satisfy a manifest checker would violate the transformer-block-only accelerator boundary.
Reusing historical operator-leaf or single-layer promotion records without current identity and certificate checks could bypass the active contamination barriers and canonical hierarchy.
Skipping directly to single-layer, multilayer, backend, or board execution would violate the three-layer repair loop and could misclassify dependency-blocked gates as hardware failures.

Shape, stream order, transfer count, memory schedule, runtime ABI, and board-wrapper consistency remain untested by the blocked operator-leaf execution; absence of evidence must not be converted into either pass claims or speculative defect claims.

A bounded loader/harness repair may be insufficient if the missing tolerance originates in the Stage6 verification contract. Any architecture, pipeline, memory-layout, numeric-policy, or major template change requires boundary-auditor escalation and approval.
Choosing tolerance after observing DUT output, loosening it during repair, or omitting max_mismatch_fraction would contaminate the golden comparison and invalidate semantic acceptance.
Changing the checkpoint, stimulus, target-model outputs, source-reference hash, or expected outputs to match the DUT would bypass the independent-reference requirement.
Treating a weight manifest or memory image as consumption proof could accept a DUT that never loaded some or all required tensors.
Retaining default or identity loader fallback could produce apparently valid traffic while bypassing real checkpoint weights.
Using whole-model scope would incorrectly require or accept embedding, final norm, LM-head/logit, or sampling work outside the Transformer-block accelerator boundary.
Editing RTL before clean functional execution could misclassify a verification-capability or loader/harness failure as a hardware defect.
Reusing prior promotion certificates or contaminated Stage7 pass fragments without exact contract-hash eligibility checks could bypass the refined semantic contract.

A loader repair that silently changes memory layout, runtime ABI, pipeline structure, numeric format, trusted templates, or architecture would exceed the bounded repair authority and require approval/backtracking.
Running connected-layer or board-level verification before operator-leaf semantic closure would violate the three-layer repair hierarchy.
At board level, substituting a simplified AXI/DDR wrapper for the exact user sample-project wrapper would invalidate deployment evidence even if the simplified simulation passed.
Numeric comparison cannot pass under the current contract because explicit tolerance fields are absent; any locally invented value would contaminate the golden policy.
Copying expected checkpoint/reference hashes into the manifest without hashing the actual bound artifacts could make a wrong-checkpoint package appear consistent.

Including model-tail tensors in DUT coverage or golden boundaries would violate the Transformer-block-only accelerator scope; omitting any required Transformer-block tensor would leave coverage incomplete.
A complete catalog, manifest existence, or memory image alone can be mistaken for consumption proof unless executed loader/DUT read evidence is required for every bound tensor.
Loader packing, tensor order, offset, length, address, dtype, or shape disagreement with Stage5 memory layout can survive manifest-only checks and produce a later value failure.

If fallback disabling or per-tensor instrumentation is not exposed by the trusted template library, attempting to patch RTL would exceed this role and require a major-template or architecture decision.
Regenerating semantic-testbench sources may change hashes. Any conflict with immutable Stage6 testbench identities requires controlled contract reissuance, not silent hash replacement.
Using contamination-barred Stage7 artifacts or historical promotion certificates as validated evidence could improperly skip the operator-leaf layer.
Board-level work performed later against a substitute wrapper would invalidate deployment evidence even if the current binding repair succeeds.
Editing only the weight manifest labels could conceal rather than repair checkpoint, scope, tensor-coverage, or consumption defects.
Reusing a sampled tensor subset or treating file existence as complete weight evidence would permit unverified weights to reach the DUT.
Inventing tolerance values, loosening tolerance after failure, changing the expected output, or regenerating a reference from changed inputs would contaminate the verification contract.

Generating expected outputs randomly, from RTL output, or through identity/default behavior would invalidate functional correctness evidence. Random generation is permitted only for deterministic input stimulus.
A loader/harness repair that alters architecture, pipeline structure, memory layout, runtime ABI, or a major trusted template exceeds automatic repair authority and requires approval.
Running single-layer, multilayer, AXI/DDR, synthesis, implementation, or board runtime before current operator-leaf promotion would violate the required three-layer repair loop.
At board level, use of any wrapper other than the exact user-supplied sample-project wrapper and source hashes would invalidate board evidence; board work is not eligible in the current repair scope.
Stale historical certificates or contaminated Stage7 outputs could be accidentally consumed as validated inputs unless the retry envelope and barrier checks enforce revision identity.
Because leaf functional tools were not_run, proposing an arithmetic RTL change now would be symptom-driven and causally unsupported.
